summary: Hirolon, the ring of the giants: a sovereign High Chief and his council of clan chiefs, the cairn-keepers and the memory of the crossings, the giant host and the price of stone.

lake_council.name: The Council of Chiefs
lake_council.desc: A High Chief and his council of clan chiefs, who govern slowly and honestly.

lake_council_2.name: Council of Stone
lake_council_2.desc: Decisions cut into a great stone: few care to argue with it.

memory_of_the_crossings_spirit.name: Memory of the Crossings
memory_of_the_crossings_spirit.desc: The giants carried the allied hosts in the First Age, and still carry strangers over streams.

giants_stride.name: The Stride
giants_stride.desc: A league in a quarter-hour, without tiring.

giants_stride_2.name: The Host of Hirolon
giants_stride_2.desc: The giants muster as a single host, and cross a country before the news of their marching.

shield_of_giants_spirit.name: Shield of Giants
shield_of_giants_spirit.desc: Shields three times a man's height in a line: little passes, nothing passes through.

war_chiefs_spirit.name: War-Chiefs
war_chiefs_spirit.desc: Chiefs trained to command a host that cannot be told to hurry.

lake_boats_spirit.name: Boats of Maruunos
lake_boats_spirit.desc: Great boats of oak carry giants and stone alike.

giants_wake.name: The Giants Wake
giants_wake.desc: The great kin are awake, and are not in a patient mood.

the_crossings_remembered.title: The Crossings Remembered
the_crossings_remembered.desc: The Keepers of the Crossings sing of the old crossings, when the giants of Hirolon bore the allied hosts over rivers in flood. The song is long and slow, and the council hears it out in a silence that fills the hall.

hiloron_trade.title: Stone from Hirolon
hiloron_trade.desc: Hirolon offers Novez a better price for its stone, on the condition that Novez sends its wool and its grain in the same boats. The counsellors weigh the offer against their own quarries.

focuses.name: The Council of Chiefs
focuses.desc: The High Chief of Hirolon rules with a council of clan chiefs, chosen by the cairn-keepers and answerable to nobody beyond the ring. They govern slowly and honestly, in a hall built for those who stoop under no door.

focuses.name: Chiefs of the Clan Halls
focuses.desc: Each clan hall on the upper slopes sends its chief to Torunalos, and each chief brings a retinue of a dozen giants. The hall is crowded, and the debates are short.

focuses.name: The Long Memory
focuses.desc: The giants remember the crossings of the First Age war, when their forebears carried the allied hosts across rivers on their shoulders. The Keepers of the Crossings sing it every year.

focuses.name: Council of Stone
focuses.desc: The council's decisions are cut into a great stone beside the cairn-fields, so that any giant may read them by passing. Few care to argue with a stone.

focuses.name: Law of the Ring
focuses.desc: The clan halls agree a single law of the ring: free passage on the giants' paths, fair weights at the Grano Saddle and a quarrel judged by three chiefs, never by one.

focuses.name: The Council Endures
focuses.desc: The council has sat in the same hall at Torunalos for a thousand years. It does not expect to move, and it does not intend to be hurried.

focuses.name: Memory of the Crossings
focuses.desc: The giants carried the allied hosts across the rivers of the First Age, and the memory has become a point of honour. A giant of Hirolon will carry any stranger across any stream, and expect no thanks.

focuses.name: Songs of the Alliance
focuses.desc: Giants sing the old songs of the alliance in the long evenings, in voices that rattle the rafters. The songs are about friendship, crossing rivers and the quality of bread.

focuses.name: Keepers of the Old Ways
focuses.desc: The Keepers of the Crossings guard the lore of the giants: the names of fords, the words of oaths and the shape of the old war. They write it on stone and recite it from memory.

focuses.name: The First Men Remembered
focuses.desc: The giants recall the First Men, who fought beside them in the old war and whose line was said to have ended. The Keepers are no longer quite so sure that it did.

focuses.name: Hear the Stranger
focuses.desc: A stranger stands before the council and warns them of a darkness in the south. The giants hear him out in silence, as they hear everything, and then begin to count their stones.

focuses.name: An Old Debt Repaid
focuses.desc: The giants carried the First Men once, across the river that could not be crossed. They will carry the Heir now, and the debt is paid in the only coin they trust.

focuses.name: The Giant Host
focuses.desc: The giants of Hirolon are few, and each of them is worth a company of men. When the council calls them they come down from the clan halls in their stone-nailed boots, and the earth shakes.

focuses.name: Hurlers of Stone
focuses.desc: A giant can throw a boulder a hundred paces with the casual flick of one arm. A company of them behind a wall is a siege-engine that does not need winding.

focuses.name: Great Mauls
focuses.desc: The giants carry mauls of oak shod in iron, taller than a man and heavier than a horse. A strike from one is a thing felt in the next valley.

focuses.name: The Stride
focuses.desc: A giant covers a league in a quarter-hour, and does not tire. The host of Hirolon can cross a country before the news of its marching.

focuses.name: Shield of Giants
focuses.desc: Shields of oak from the Hiloron Woods, three times a man's height and bound in iron, are carried in a line by giants side by side. Little passes them, and nothing passes through.

focuses.name: War-Chiefs
focuses.desc: War-Chief Gorrum the Tall schools a company of chiefs in the art of commanding a host that cannot be told to hurry. They learn that a giant moves when he agrees to, and not before.

focuses.name: The Host of Hirolon
focuses.desc: On the council's word the giants muster as a single host, stone against iron as in the old songs. It is small, and nothing stands before it for long.

focuses.name: Cairn and Quarry
focuses.desc: The Grano gives stone and the valleys of Tirlan give bread, and the giants have learned to turn the one into silver to pay for the other. The council takes care that nobody forgets it.

focuses.name: The Quarries
focuses.desc: New galleries are driven into the Grano quarry faces, and the giants haul out blocks that no cart could carry. The Golden Court wants the stone for Parim's quays, and has begun to haggle over the price.

focuses.name: Boats of Maruunos
focuses.desc: Great boats of oak ply from Maruunos at the Hilorn mouth, built to carry giants as easily as stone. A passing merchant would mistake one for a barn on the water.

focuses.name: Stone Roads
focuses.desc: The giants lay roads of great flat stones, each a cartload by itself. Such a road will outlast every empire that crosses it.

focuses.name: Trade with Novez
focuses.desc: Hirolon's neighbour Novez has long bought its stone from the giants at a price that both find irritating. The council offers a better arrangement.

focuses.name: A Rich Ring
focuses.desc: Stone, strength for hire and the trade of the Saddle make Hirolon the richest hill country of the south-west. The giants spend their wealth on better boats and heavier hammers, which is what giants do.

focuses.name: The Cairn Treaty
focuses.desc: The Cairn Treaty, sworn on the day the dominions took their charters, binds Hirolon to the crown as a friend and not as a subject. The giants have honoured it for centuries, and expect the same of Parim.

focuses.name: Giants for Hire
focuses.desc: Under the treaty Hirolon lends a few of its giants to the crown's works and hosts, in places where one giant is worth a company. The Royal Army finds them hard to feed and very hard to replace.

focuses.name: The Giants Wake
focuses.desc: The council has called the great kin from the quarries and the clan halls. The giants have woken, and they are not in a patient mood.

focuses.name: Stones Against the Dead
focuses.desc: Boulders thrown by giants break the dead as they break anything: into smaller pieces. The giants fight the hosts of the grave with the same stolid method they bring to quarrying.

focuses.name: The Ring Holds
focuses.desc: Walls of giant-cut stone rise across the Hilorn Gap and the Grano Saddle, each block the size of a cottage. If Hirolon is to fall, it will take a great while.

focuses.name: Treaty and Shield
focuses.desc: Hirolon reaffirms the Cairn Treaty and offers the Lost Cause a company of its great kin. The giants do not forget a bargain, and the Golden King is held to his half.

focuses.name: Hirolon Endures
focuses.desc: The war is over, the ring is quiet and the great kin go back to their quarries. The council sits again in the old hall, and the Keepers sing the crossings once more.

focuses.name: The Eldest Cairn
focuses.desc: The Eldest Cairn stands highest of all the cairn-fields, and a keeper adds one stone to it each year, as the keepers before him did. The High Chief asks the keepers, for the first time anyone can recall, what it is that they are counting.

focuses.name: Stone for Stone
focuses.desc: The keepers set out their terms for anyone who comes to ask about the count: a levy to haul cut stone to the cairn-fields, ships lent for a season, and no army of the asker inside the ring for as long as the bargain holds.

focuses.name: Speak the Count
focuses.desc: The keepers agree to say aloud how many stones the Eldest Cairn holds, and where the long dikes stood before the sea came over them, to any seeker who has kept the bargain. It is more than the giants have told men in all the years since.

focuses.name: Keep the Silence
focuses.desc: The keepers will say only what they have always said, that the land was asked for too much. The count stays in the stones, and the ring keeps its own counsel as it has done since before Aen.
